description.value: The study combined structural and functional MRI to investigate how amygdalar atrophy in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia affects emotion-related activity in face-responsive regions.

spans.text: By combining structural and functional MRI in 19 patients with bvFTD and 20 controls we investigated the neural effects of emotion in face-responsive cortex and its relationship with amygdalar gray matter (GM) volume in neurodegeneration.

description.value: A case-control study of patients with bvFTD and healthy controls, using structural MRI and an event-related fMRI experiment.

spans.text: We used a two emotion (fearful, chewing) × two modality (intact, scrambled) factorial event-related fMRI-design.

spans.text: In the control group we found a significantly higher PSC for fearful compared to chewing expressions when contrasted with their respective scrambled versions in three of the four defined face-responsive regions, i.e., in left FFA [ t (19) = −2.605, p = .009, 1-tailed], left pSTS [ t (19) = −3.045, p = .003, 1-tailed] and right pSTS [ t (19) = −2.910, p = .004, 1-tailed] but not in right FFA [ t (19) = −1.470, p = .08, 1-tailed].

value: Controls showed significantly higher percent signal change for fearful than chewing expressions, contrasted with their respective scrambled versions, in the left FFA, left pSTS and right pSTS, but not in the right FFA. The bvFTD group did not show a significant difference in any of these regions.

value: Within the bvFTD group, left amygdalar gray matter volume correlated positively with emotion-related percent signal change in the left FFA. The association was specific to the amygdala rather than the hippocampus and was driven by gray matter volume in the basolateral and superficial amygdala subregions, but not the centromedial amygdala.
